clue.text: A strapless top is a mistake underground

parts.note: a boob is a blunder or silly mistake
the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a strapless top is an error made on the Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob tube is a close-fitting strapless garment covering the chest, a common British name for a bandeau top.

clue.text: Billy makes a sound partner in Britten work

definitions.text: Billy makes a sound partner in Britten work

indicators.note: making a sound tells us to listen to the word for partner rather than read its spelling

parts.note: bud is American slang for a pal or partner

explanation.surface: Billy turns out to be a fine companion in a piece by Benjamin Britten.
explanation.walkthrough: Britten's opera Billy Budd gives Billy his partner in the title; that surname is said just like BUD, a mate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britten's opera title, the name paired with Billy is the sailor's surname, so it is literally Billy's partner in that work.

clue.text: Well-produced paintings?

parts.note: read as pictures produced by a well, i.e. what gushes from oil wells, which also names a kind of painting

explanation.surface: A gallery boasts of its finely made pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings done in oil paint are called by the medium's name, and the same substance is what wells are drilled to produce.

clue.text: Exciting time in fieldwork

indicators.note: in places the time unit inside the farming word

parts.note: tilling is working the soil of a field
hr is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time

explanation.surface: A spell of farm labour proves surprisingly exciting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrilling gives a strong sense of excitement, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Bosom pals bid afresh for dangerous job

indicators.note: doing something afresh means rearranging it anew, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Close friends make a new offer for a hazardous piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Defusing and removing unexploded bombs is a famously hazardous occupation for army specialists.

clue.text: Relish Tom's being at university

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, so tom's gives cat's
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Tom is enjoying himself now he has gone up to college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' looks like a verb but is the noun for a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Catsup is an old variant spelling of ketchup, a tomato relish or sauce.

clue.text: Wool drops a point in the market

indicators.note: drops means the wool loses one of its letters

parts.note: angora is wool from the Angora goat or rabbit
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Wool falls by a point in trading on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a price falling one point; 'drops' actually takes N, a compass point, out of ANGORA.
explanation.definitionFit: An agora was the open marketplace and assembly area of an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Adore ITMA's funny style of broadcasting

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd or peculiar, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words are taken as written, including the S

explanation.surface: A fan says they love the comic style of the old radio show ITMA.
explanation.walkthrough: ITMA (It's That Man Again) was a wartime BBC radio comedy, apt for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam radio is a jocular term for old-fashioned sound broadcasting, as opposed to television.

clue.text: Round trip organised by guide leader that's appearing proud

indicators.note: organised means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A guide in charge has arranged a return journey and looks pleased with herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proud' here means sticking out, as a nail stands proud of a surface, not pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud can mean projecting above a surface, so something protruding is appearing proud.

clue.text: Barrels found around ancient dumps

indicators.note: around tells us the containers enclose the word for ancient

parts.note: drums are cylindrical containers like barrels
ancient means old

explanation.surface: Containers are discovered on old rubbish tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumps' looks like rubbish heaps, but it is the low mood of 'down in the dumps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the doldrums means being in low spirits, just as being in the dumps does.

clue.text: Surrender because of one's self-image?

parts.note: for can mean because of, as in jumping for joy
the ego is one's sense of self

explanation.surface: Someone gives up a position out of vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: To forego (or forgo) something is to give it up or relinquish it, so it means surrender.

clue.text: Not to pay it would diminish one's credit

definitions.text: Not to pay it would diminish one's credit

parts.words: Not to pay it would diminish one's credit
parts.note: the surface sounds financial, but credit here is reputation: the obligation in question is one of honour, like a gambling debt

explanation.surface: Failing to settle a sum would lower a person's credit rating.
explanation.definitionFit: Such an obligation cannot be enforced by law, so only your honour and good name suffer if you default.

clue.text: Oversized nutcracker?

parts.note: alludes to the saying about using an excessively heavy tool to crack a nut

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget is far too big for its purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Using a massive hammer to crack a nut is the stock image of applying wildly excessive force.

clue.text: See girl on coach but fail to take opportunity

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
a coach is a long-distance bus, giving the bus

explanation.surface: Someone spots a young woman on a coach but lets the chance slip.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts MISS above THE BUS; 'See' is just a link inviting us to look.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss the bus is an idiom for failing to seize a chance while it is available.

clue.text: Graceful in progress through air, one lit on tree perhaps

indicators.note: in places the word for graceful inside the word for travel through the air

parts.note: flight is movement through the air
airy can mean light and graceful in manner

explanation.surface: A dancer moves gracefully through the air, one flying past a lit-up tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A small decorative electric lamp, typically strung on a Christmas tree, is called by this name.

clue.text: I spoil one sort of Japanese porcelain

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to ruining a piece of fine Japanese china.
explanation.definitionFit: Imari ware is a style of richly decorated Japanese porcelain named after its export port.

clue.text: Undertake to get firm under control

parts.note: jelly or concrete sets when it gets firm
in hand means under control

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to take on the job of bringing a company under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company, but it is the adjective in 'get firm'.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something in hand is to begin or undertake it.

clue.text: Mother insured for working outside — her charges are small

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters wrap around the word for mother
working means in operation, a reworking, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother takes out insurance for her job, though the fees she charges are low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working outside' splits: 'working' turns INSURED into NURSEID and 'outside' puts that round MA. 'charges' looks like fees but means children in her care.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny looks after young children, so those in her charge are small.

clue.text: Shoulders no responsibility?

parts.note: a person who declines to shoulder a duty dismisses it with a movement of the shoulders

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to carry any responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss something as unimportant is shown by raising the shoulders, a gesture of indifference.

clue.text: Put curb around gelding's head to prevail

indicators.note: around tells us the restraint goes round the letter taken

parts.note: a rein is a check or curb

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rider puts a bridle on a gelded horse to gain the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to hold sway or predominate, so it can mean prevail.

clue.text: Drunk in mid-Atlantic?

definitions.meaning: an old British idiom for tipsy or intoxicated
literally, a ship halfway across the ocean has covered part of the seas

explanation.surface: A sailor is intoxicated far out in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means drunk, from a ship halfway through its voyage, and literally fits a mid-ocean position.

clue.text: Use spades to trim off excess

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
to pare is to trim off the outer edge

explanation.surface: A gardener uses spades to cut back overgrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare as a noun is something extra kept in reserve, i.e. a surplus.

clue.text: Band call

definitions.meaning: a circle such as a wedding hoop or encircling strip

explanation.definitionFit: A ring is a circular band, and to ring someone is to phone them.

clue.text: Watch open-mouthed as winger initially moves into space

indicators.note: moves into tells us the letter enters the opening

parts.note: a gap is a space

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter

explanation.surface: Fans stare as a wide player runs into an open area of the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface makes 'winger' a player; it only supplies W.
explanation.definitionFit: To gawp is to stare stupidly with the mouth open.

clue.text: He has no choice, poor chap

definitions.meaning: from the proverb that those who ask for alms cannot be choosers
a destitute man who asks for charity

explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant is proverbially unable to choose, and is literally an impoverished fellow.

clue.text: Reproduction of a man's oil painting

indicators.note: a reproduction is a copy made anew, here a rearrangement of the letters

parts.note: the letters of these words are taken as written, including the S

explanation.surface: Someone owns a copy of a man's oil painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait in the Louvre is perhaps the world's most famous painting.

clue.text: Model one can't stand?

definitions.meaning: someone who poses for an artist
humorously, a person who is seated rather than standing

explanation.definitionFit: An artist's model is one who poses, and one who sits is literally not standing.

clue.text: The difference between imports and exports

definitions.text: The difference between imports and exports

parts.words: The difference between imports and exports
parts.note: a plain description of the shortfall in a country's balance of goods

explanation.surface: An economist defines a trade measure.
explanation.definitionFit: The excess of imports over exports is the deficit in a nation's balance of trade.
